SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No. TRY
                              325
Special Branch 2 Division, H.Q.
REPORT                        Date August 25, 1940.

Subject Communication dated July 31, 1940 from H. B. M. Consulate-
        General.

Made by D.S.I. Pitts.         Forwarded by D.S.I. Logan

In regard to the contents of the
attached communication which states that the 22
individuals named therein are believed to be
refugees from Europe, enquiries reveal that such
is not the case, the majority of these persons
having been domiciled in Shanghai or China for
many years. Many of the persons named are German
Aryans and to secure their passport details is now
a matter of impossibility. The following
information, however, is submitted with regard
to the individuals mentioned:-

(1) T.O. SCHMID, Swiss citizen, manager of Anderson,
    Clayton & Co., 34 Avenue
    Edward VII. Very respectable
    person and very wealthy.
    Resides at 251 Columbia
    Circle with his wife. Mixes
    freely in local American
    circles.

(2) A. DIERKING, stateless, formerly a German. Renounced
    his German nationality many
    years ago and for some time
    served in the British Navy.
    Is the father-in-law of Mr.
    H. L. GIBSON, British, of
    30/865 Yu Yuen Road. DIERKING
    is pro-British in his outlook.

(3) Johann Willy SCHULTZ, no details available.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。    档案号 TRY
                              325
总部特别分部二科
报告                          日期：1940年8月25日。

事由：英国驻华总领事馆1940年7月31日来函。

由特别分部督察皮茨（Pitts）拟写。    由特别分部督察洛根（Logan）转呈

关于所附信函的内容，该信称其中列名的22人据信为来自欧洲的难民，经查询，事实并非如此，这些人中的大多数已在上海或中国居住多年。许多列名人士为德国雅利安人，目前无法获取其护照详情。然而，现就提及的个人提交如下信息：-

(1) T.O. SCHMID，瑞士公民，安德森·克莱顿公司（Anderson, Clayton & Co.）经理，地址为爱德华七世路34号。为人非常正派且十分富有。与其妻居住在哥伦比亚圈251号。与当地美国人圈子交往 freely。

(2) A. DIERKING，无国籍人士，原为德国人。多年前已放弃德国国籍，并曾在英国海军服役一段时间。是居住在豫园路30/865号的英国人H. L. GIBSON先生的岳父。DIERKING持亲英观点。

(3) Johann Willy SCHULTZ，无详细资料。

S.B. REGISTRY
325
No.
Date 27 / 8 / 40

August 27, 40.

Dear Mr. Lamb,

In reply to your letter dated July 31, 1940,
I forward herewith a copy of a Police report regarding
those individuals named in the list and of whom the
Police have some record.

I must apologize for the delay in forwarding
this information but, as you observe, the majority of
the individuals listed are of reputable character and
it is much more difficult to obtain reliable information
regarding law-abiding citizens than those whose activities
frequently or generally come to the notice of the Police.

Yours sincerely,

L. M. Lamb, Esq.,
Superintending Consul,
H.B.M. Consulate-General,
Shanghai.
